1 Important Information for Tentative Rulings and Hearings:
1. Please review and follow the Tentative Ruling Instructions which can be found on the Court’s website
using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/unified-family-court/ufc-tentative-rulings.
2. If you wish to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, you must notify the other party
(unless there is a restraining order in place) and the Court Clerk in the Department where the hearing
is scheduled of your objection by 4:00 PM the Court day prior to the hearing date. Court days do not
include Court holidays, Saturdays, or Sundays. The Court’s Holiday Schedule can be found on the
Court’s website using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/general-information/holiday-
schedules.
3. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 403 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
please call (415) 551–3741 or send an email to Department403@sftc.org.
4. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 404 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
please call (415) 551–3744 or send an email to Department404@sftc.org.
5. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 416 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
please call (415) 551– 3756 or send an email to Department416@sftc.org.
6. When you contact the Court Clerk to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, please
specify the paragraph(s) and / or line number(s) of the Tentative Ruling which contains the language
to which you object.
7. You may appear at your hearing either (a) in-person; (b) by video; or (c) by phone. Pursuant to SFLR
11.7(D)(4), if you choose to appear by video or phone, you must be continuously connected to Zoom
from 8:50 a.m. until 12:00 p.m. or until your hearing is concluded (or from 1:20 p.m. until 4:30 p.m.
or until your hearing is concluded, if your hearing is scheduled to start at 1:30 p.m.). If you fail to
appear in-person, by video, or phone, the Court may proceed with the hearing in your absence. The
Court is not required to contact you before your hearing.
8. If you choose to appear by video or by phone, you must comply with the Notice and Instructions for
Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth below.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER RE: ATTORNEY FEES AND COSTS, AND TIER-2 MEDIATION IN
13 ADVANCE OF TRIAL
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
16 Court makes the following findings and orders:
17 A. Procedural History
18 1) The parties are Petitioner David Battenfield (Father) and Respondent Micah Bishop (Mother).
19 2) They share one minor child: Maxwell (DOB: 7/27/26).
20 3) On 12/9/25, Mother filed a Request for Order seeking a Tier II Interview of the minor child’s
21 therapist and teacher and $50,000 in Family Code section 2030 attorney’s fees and costs in
22 advance of trial set for 5/19/26, 5/20/26, 5/21/26, and 5/26/26 in Dept. 405 on the issue of
23 custody and visitation and Father’s move-away request (couched in terms of whether the minor
24 child will attend school in San Francisco or Redding). Mother asserts there is a significant
25 disparity in the parties’ financial situations as evidenced by the parties’ respective equity in their
26 homes, retirement assets, and incomes. Mother states Father has representation for trial and
27 Mother cannot afford it.
28 4) On 12/9/25, Mother filed a supportive Memorandum of Points and Authorities.
1 5) On 12/9/25, Mother’s consulting attorney filed a declaration substantiating her attorney’s fees
2 request.
3 6) On 12/9/25, Mother filed an Income and Expense Declaration.
4 7) On 2/10/26, Father filed a Responsive Declaration in opposition to Mother’s Request for Order.
5 Father asserts the Court already denied Mother’s request for a Tier II Interview of the minor
6 child’s therapist and teacher. Father further asserts that he does not have the ability to pay
7 Mother’s attorney’s fees and costs given that that he lost his full-time job on 10/31/25 and is
8 currently working as an independent architect. Father states he has accrued $85,500 in credit card
9 debt as a result. Father believes Mother already incurred excessive attorney’s fees ($150,000) as
10 demonstrated by Father incurring only $70,000 in fees. Father asserts that Mother misrepresented
11 her financial resources. Father alleges Mother is to blame for the high level of litigation in this
12 matter.
13 8) On 2/10/26, Father filed a supportive Memorandum of Points and Authorities.
14 9) On 2/10/26, Father filed an Income and Expense Declaration.
15 10) On 2/19/26, Mother filed a Reply Declaration reiterating her requests. Mother asserts that her
16 Income and Expense Declaration is accurate and alleges that Father has undisclosed income.
17 Mother further asserts that she is also carrying credit card debt and debt to her parents. Mother
18 states, “I have maintained that neither of us can afford this constant litigation.” Mother alleges
19 Father is to blame for the high level of litigation in this matter.
20 B. Findings and Order
21 1) On 11/4/25, the Court denied Mother’s request for a Tier II Interview of the minor child’s
22 therapist and teacher and set the matter on the trial setting calendar. See Minute Order from
23 hearing on 11/4/25. Accordingly, Mother’s request for a Tier II Interview of the minor child’s
24 therapist and teacher is DENIED.
25 2) Counsel for Father is admonished for failing to prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing on
26 11/4/25 and shall prepare the order forthwith.
27 3) Mother’s request for Family Code section 2030 attorney’s fees is GRANTED; albeit in the
28 amount of $35,000 as the Court finds there is a disparity in income and access to funds to retain
29 or maintain counsel.
1 4) The Court further finds that Father has or is reasonably likely to have the ability to pay $35,000
2 towards Mother’s legal representation while maintaining his own based on the documentary
3 evidence Mother submitted of Father’s Charles Schwab account with a balance of $1,091,023.01
4 as of September 2024. See Exhibit B of Mother’s 12/9/25 Request for Order.
5 5) The Court cannot find that Father has the ability to pay above $35,000 in Mother’s legal fees as
6 the Court understands that Father lost his full-time employment as of 10/31/25 and has had to rely
7 on his retirement accounts to pay his own expenses. The Court also considers Father’s age and
8 Mother’s concession that neither party can afford the cost of litigation when analyzing Father’s
9 ability to pay Mother’s legal fees from his retirement accounts.
10 6) Finally, the Court finds $35,000 is reasonable and necessary given that the parties are set for trial
11 on 5/19/26, 5/20/26, 5/21/26, and 5/26/26.
12 7) Father shall balance this balance in full by 4/8/26 and shall be fully responsible for any tax
13 penalties incurred as a result of this attorney’s fee award.
14 8) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner/Mother Virginia C. Chatham and Respondent/Father Reggio Hearn.
18 The parties have two minor children subject to these proceedings: Reggio Hearn Jr. (DOB:
19 09/26/11) and Jeanne Hearn (DOB: 09/26/11).
20 2) On October 10, 2025, Mother filed a Request for Order seeking orders related to selecting the
21 children’s school and holiday schedule.
22 3) On December 11, 2025, Father filed an Opposition to Petitioner’s Request for Order re: Selection
23 of Children’s Schools and Holiday Travel Schedule, which has been read and considered by the
24 Court.
25 4) On February 19, 2026, Mother filed a Reply Declaration, which has been read and considered by
26 the Court.
27 B. Findings and Order
28 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
29 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
1 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
2 child(ren) is the United States.
3 2) Commencing the 2026-2027 academic school year, Father shall select which high school the
4 minor child Reggio will attend. Mother shall promptly cooperate in signing all required school
5 forms necessary to effectuate Father’s school selection.
6 3) Commencing the 2026-2027 academic school year, Mother shall select which high school the
7 minor child Jeanne will attend. Father shall promptly cooperate in signing all required school
8 forms necessary to effectuate Mother’s school selection.
9 4) Mother’s contribution for each child’s tuition expense shall be capped at $15,000.00 per
10 academic year. Father shall be financially responsible for the remaining tuition expense for each
11 minor child beyond Mother’s $15,000.00 annual contribution (i.e., cap).
12 5) School breaks that are one week in duration are hereby defined as Monday through Friday of the
13 school break with each parent continuing to have their respective weekends.
14 6) Mother’s Day and Father’s Day are defined as 4:00 p.m. on Saturday through 5:00 p.m. on
15 Sunday.
16 7) When school is not in session, the exchange time shall be 3:00 p.m. on Fridays.
17 8) All travel with the minor children shall occur during each parent’s allotted parenting time. There
18 will be no extension of time for either parent beyond the days/times ordered by the Court without
19 the agreement of the other parent. Two weeks of vacation is defined as no more than 14
20 consecutive days.
21 9) There will be no deviation from the week on/week off schedule during 3-day weekends. The
22 three-day weekend will automatically go to the parent who has care and custody of the children
23 during their respective week.
24 10) All prior orders not in conflict with this order shall remain in full force and effect.
25 11) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner Danielle Taylor and Respondent Cheick Diarra. Per the Petition for
18 Dissolution of Marriage filed 3/29/24 and the Response and Request for Dissolution of Marriage
19 filed 5/22/24, the parties married on 7/11/11 and separated on 2/1/24, for a marriage of 12 years
20 and 6 months. They have no minor children in common.
21 2) On 12/12/25, Respondent filed a Request for Order seeking monetary sanctions in the amount of
22 $6,065.95 against Petitioner and Attorney Matthew Scherling under Family Code section 271,
23 Code of Civil Procedure section 2030.010, and California Rules of Court, rule 5.425. Respondent
24 asserts that Attorney Matthew Scherling caused unnecessary delay in the proceedings, misused
25 the discovery process, and made unauthorized appearances in this action.
26 3) On 12/12/25, Respondent filed a Proof of Service indicating both Petitioner and Attorney
27 Matthew Scherling were served on 12/12/25 by email.
28 4) Petitioner did not file a Responsive Declaration.
29 5) The Court docket reflects no Notice of Limited Scope Representation (form FL-950) was filed.
1 B. Findings and Order
2 1) Attorney Matthew Scherling shall forthwith file a Notice of Limited Scope Representation (form
3 FL-950) as this is a mandatory requirement under California Rules of Court, rule 5.425 and the
4 Court docket reflects no Notice of Limited Scope Representation (form FL-190) was filed.
5 2) Nevertheless, the Court finds that Respondent was in no way prejudiced by this error as
6 Respondent himself attached as Exhibit B to his 12/12/25 Request for Order an email exchange
7 between Attorney Matthew Scherling and Respondent that acknowledges Attorney Matthew
8 Scherling’s limited scope representation and references an attached Notice of Limited Scope
9 Representation (form FL-950) which is signed by Attorney Matthew Scherling and Petitioner.
10 3) The Court further finds that neither evidence of conduct subject to sanctions under Code of Civil
11 Procedure section 2030.010 nor evidence of Attorney Matthew Scherling’s conduct causing
12 unnecessary delay was presented.
13 4) Based on the foregoing, Respondent’s request is DENIED.
14 5) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

15 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
16 Court makes the following findings and orders:
17 A. Procedural History
18 1) On 06/23/25 Petitioner/Father filed a Request for Order seeking sole legal and sole physical
19 custody of the minor children. Father requests that Respondent/Mother have reasonable visitation
20 with the children, alleging that they are not doing well in Mother’s care. Father states that the
21 parties’ daughter told him she no longer wanted to live with Mother. Father requests a Tier II
22 interview of the children.
23 2) On 08/01/25, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration wherein she alleges that their daughter is
24 upset because Mother’s household is strict and when she does not like Mother’s rules, she calls
25 Father crying. Mother states their daughter wants to pursue a relationship with a boy and Mother
26 is fearful that she will become pregnant. Mother alleges that Father has not complied with the
27 Court’s orders from 11/21/24 and that his motion should be denied, until such time as he
28 complies with the Court order.
1 3) The Court notes that on 11/21/24 the parties attended mediation and reached a stipulation which
2 provides:
3 a. Father shall establish family therapy for the minor children and father. Father shall
4 inform Mother of family therapist and first session.
5 b. Once minor children are ready, Father shall have one day visit a week.
6 c. Final stage, Father shall have alternating weekends with the minor children.
7 d. All other times not mentioned, the minor children shall be under the care and control of
8 Mother. Mother currently has sole legal (01/16/25) and sole physical custody (11/21/24).
9 4) On 10/23/25, the Court granted Father’s request for a Tier II interview of both minor children to
10 determine if, in fact, they are being mistreated in Mother’s home. The matter was set for review
11 hearing on 12/11/25 for consideration of the Tie II report.
12 5) On 12/11/25, the Court continued the matter to 2/26/26 to allow additional time for a Tier II
13 report. The Court indicated this would be the last continuance.
14 B. Findings and Order
15 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
16 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
17 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
18 child(ren) is the United States.
19 2) As of 2/23/26, the Court has not yet received a Tier II report from Family Court Services. The
20 matter is hereby dropped from the Court’s calendar. No further review hearings will be scheduled
21 on this issue.
22 3) All existing orders shall remain in full force and effect.
23 4) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner Alberta Babygirl Stanley and Respondent Dion Horatio Stanley.
18 2) On 4/22/25, Petitioner filed a Petition for Dissolution of Marriage indicating the date of marriage
19 is 3/1/95 and date of separation is 6/29/97 for a marriage of 2 years and 9 months. There is no
20 Proof of Service on file indicating the Petition for Dissolution of Marriage was served on
21 Respondent.
22 3) On 11/24/25, Petitioner filed an Application for Order for Posting of the Summons (Family Law)
23 (form FL-110) at the San Francisco Superior Court. Petitioner asserts she last had contact with
24 Respondent on 6/29/97 when “Respondent gave me back our kids and we never saw each other
25 again.” Petitioner states that Respondent never worked when the parties were together, so he
26 doesn’t have a work address.
27 4) On 11/24/25, Petitioner filed a supportive declaration attesting to the ways in which Petitioner
28 attempted to locate Respondent, including:
29 a. Calling Respondent’s last known phone number, which is no longer in service;
1 b. Speaking to the parties’ two adult children who do not know where Respondent is
2 (Respondent also has a sister though Petitioner do not know who she is and is not aware
3 of any other family members of Respondent);
4 c. Calling the telephone directory of San Francisco;
5 d. Checking the tax records at the San Francisco County Clerk’s Office;
6 e. Checking voter registration;
7 f. Calling the Department of Child Support (who could not provide information since the
8 parties no longer have minor children);
9 g. Checking Facebook and Instagram; and
10 h. Checking Respondent’s last known address.
11 5) On 11/24/25, Petitioner filed a Request for Order seeking alternative service which references
12 Petitioner’s Application for Order for Posting.
13 B. Findings and Order
14 1) Per California Rules of Court, rule 5.72, when Respondent cannot be located for service of
15 summons by any method described in Code of Civil Procedure sections 415.10 - 415.40,
16 Petitioner may request an order for service by publication or posting under Code of Civil
17 Procedure sections 415.50 and 413.30.
18 2) Since service by publication or posting is the least likely of approved service methods to give
19 Respondent actual notice of the proceeding “reasonable diligence” is required. Code of Civil
20 Procedure sections 415.50 and 413.30.
21 3) Petitioner's alleged “actual ignorance” of Respondent's location does not suffice as “reasonable
22 diligence.” Rather, Petitioner must make a showing of exhaustive attempts to locate Respondent
23 through a thorough, systematic, and good faith investigation. (Olvera v. Olvera (1991) 232 CA3d
24 32, 41-42.)
25 4) Under California Rules of Court, rule 5.72, service of summons by posting may be ordered
26 instead of service by publication only if Petitioner is eligible for a waiver of court fees and costs.
27 5) A fee waiver was granted in this case on 4/22/25; therefore, Petitioner qualifies for an order for
28 service by posting.
1 6) The Court finds that Petitioner made reasonable diligent efforts to find and serve Respondent
2 under Code of Civil Procedure section 413.30, including exhaustive attempts to locate
3 Respondent through a thorough, systematic, and good faith investigation as follows:
4 a. Calling Respondent’s last known phone number, which is no longer in service;
5 b. Speaking to the parties’ two adult children who do not know where Respondent is
6 (Respondent also has a sister though Petitioner do not know who she is and is not aware
7 of any other family members of Respondent);
8 c. Calling the telephone directory of San Francisco;
9 d. Checking the tax records at the San Francisco County Clerk’s Office;
10 e. Checking voter registration;
11 f. Calling the Department of Child Support (who could not provide information since the
12 parties no longer have minor children);
13 g. Checking Facebook and Instagram; and
14 h. Checking Respondent’s last known address.
15 7) As such, Petitioner’s Application for Order for Posting is GRANTED. Petitioner is permitted to
16 serve Respondent by posting pursuant to the terms of form FL-982 (Order for Posting), which the
17 Court will prepare and file concurrently with this order.
18 8) Once posting is completed, Petitioner shall file with the Court form FL-985 (Proof of Service by
19 Posting) which must be completed by the person who posted the documents and then filed with
20 the Court once posting is completed.
21 9) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing and Order for Posting.

15 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
16 Court makes the following findings and orders:
17 A. Procedural History
18 1) The parties in this matter are Petitioner/Father Rossni Presendieu and Respondent/Mother
19 Amanda Presendieu. The parties have one minor child: Isaiah Presendieu (06/02/24).
20 2) On November 19, 2025, Father filed an ex parte application seeking sole legal and sole physical
21 custody of the minor child, parenting time orders, and an order that the minor child immediately
22 be returned to California. The Court issued the following temporary orders:
23 a. Temporary custody to Father;
24 b. No visitation to Mother, until further order of the Court; and
25 c. An order that the minor child be returned to California no later than November 21, 2025
26 at 5:00 p.m.
27 d. Matter set further hearing on December 8, 2025.
1 3) On November 19, 2025, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration wherein she requested this Court
2 deny Father’s requests and set the matter for regular hearing. Mother seeks primary custody of
3 the minor child and permission to relocate with the minor child to Denver.
4 4) On December 8, 2025, the parties appeared on the Readiness Calendar, and the Court set the
5 matter for Family Court Services (FCS) Mediation on February 9, 2026 and ordered a return
6 hearing on February 26, 2026.
7 5) On February 17, 2026, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration wherein she requests joint legal
8 and joint physical custody with an alternating week parenting plan. However, the Court has
